text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000133 bills 99215 well above expectation in every complexity tier, including many low-complexity visits, but the few returned charts support the billed levels and are too thin to settle the question.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern leans toward upcoding. The 99215 share runs roughly two to four times the all-provider rate in every condition-count tier, not just among sicker patients, and the mix is dominated by 99214. More than a third of the 99215s fall on patients with 0–1 chronic conditions, with diagnoses such as upper respiratory infection (C0059377, C0059904), UTI (C0059547, C0059715), low back pain (C0059483) or a follow-up code alone (C0060154), which would not usually support high-complexity decision making. Against that, the records review gives no confirmation: only 3 documented 99215s came back, all documented at high MDM. The one below-billed note (C0059564) is a 99214, and the data-reviewed notes all match lab or test lines on the claim. That is too little documentation to judge either way. The supported claim C0059583 is a 42-year-old with no chronic conditions billed for abdominal pain. A reviewer should check whether its high-MDM note reflects a genuine acute workup or a templated or cloned note. The first next step is a targeted records request for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet."}
